title: Fixed 7-layer analyze known stack route (MgF2/TiO2)
scientific_hypothesis: A fixed 7-layer MgF2/TiO2 stack tests whether the proposed optical mechanism can balance the shared spectral targets, total thickness, and manufacturing robustness.
design_principle: Chirped or multi-quarter-wave design using high-index contrast pairs (TiO2/MgF2 or Ta2O5/SiO2). Using the highest available index contrast (TiO2/MgF2) maximizes bandwidth per pair, while SiO2/Ta2O5 offers better mechanical stability. This route tests the TiO2/MgF2 combination for maximum optical performance.
proposed_topology: exactly 7 finite layers from the incident side: MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2
manufacturing_considerations: Independent one-sigma thickness error of 2 nm
Common incidence-angle offset bounded by +/- 1 degree
theory_basis: Multilayer interference filters rely on constructive/destructive interference. More layers allow for broader bandwidth suppression of reflection. High index contrast allows for fewer periods to achieve the same bandwidth, but here we fix the count to 10 to test the limit of performance vs. complexity.
expected_advantages: Better angular stability due to flatter spectral response.
known_risks: Higher total physical thickness increases deposition time and stress.
Increased sensitivity to cumulative thickness errors; small deviations in many layers can compound.
TiO2 can have higher absorption or stress compared to Ta2O5/SiO2.
execution_request_english: Perform one bounded TMM thickness-optimization route for Fixed 7-layer analyze known stack route (MgF2/TiO2). Use these declared media constraints: substrate: fused-silica; ambient: air; candidate_coating_materials: MgF2, SiO2, Al2O3, Ta2O5, TiO2. Use exactly 7 finite layers from the incident side: MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2 / TiO2 / MgF2. Optimize every finite layer physical thickness with finite positive bounds. Evaluate the wavelength, incidence-angle, polarization, soft-objective, and uncertainty controls supplied below. Report verified optical metrics, total thickness, and manufacturing robustness; targets rank candidates and never gate physical validity. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees, 30 degrees, 45 degrees. polarization TE, TM. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: mean reflectance <= 0.8%; worst-case reflectance <= 3%; fewer layers; lower total physical thickness. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance. robustness conditions: independent one-sigma thickness error of 2 nm; common incidence-angle offset bounded by +/- 1 degree.
